picks.title: Meet KLING 4.0 | You Call the Shots
picks.excerpt: Kling 4.0 arrives in October with Kling 4.0 Flash live now for Ultra yearly subscribers; the model targets filmmakers with up to 30-second generations, many multimodal references and keyframe-level narrative control.
picks.rationale: Freshest and most actionable item: a major video-model release aimed at filmmakers (30-second shots, multimodal references, keyframe control). Nothing on Kling 4.0 has been published before. 'The Beat' showcase short covers the same launch, so it was dropped.

picks.title: Art of the Frame Podcast: The Alan Smithee Round Table - How will AI impact the future of filmmaking?
picks.excerpt: Scott Simmons, Katie Hinsen and Michael Kammes discuss how AI tools, unified post software and shifting economics are transforming film and TV production.
picks.rationale: Fresh, credible post-production perspective: working editors and colorists on how AI and unified post tools are changing the economics of production. It is a new episode, not the 09-08 'what we did last summer' round table.

picks.title: Dear Upstairs Neighbors: How Connie He Taught a Machine to See the Way She Draws
picks.excerpt: Pixar alum Connie He explains how she tuned custom Veo and Imagen models to reproduce her own concept art for the six-minute Tribeca short, and how animators and researchers learned to share a working language. (A new craft interview; the film itself was covered on 2026-07-02 via No Film School.)
picks.rationale: Swapped in for the Tim Thompson item (weak AI angle): a craft interview on tuning custom Veo/Imagen models to a director's own concept art — a new angle on a film covered 2026-07-02.

picks.title: 'Harry Potter' Producer David Barron Backs AI Adaptation Of 'The Call Of The Wild'
picks.excerpt: Six-time Harry Potter producer David Barron is producing a generative-AI adaptation of Jack London's The Call of the Wild, written and directed by Simon Rumley, with prompting and technical work led by the team at nmatic. Barron argues the novel's epic Alaskan scale and dog-and-wolf fights were previously impossible to film faithfully.
picks.rationale: Recovery-pass backfill. A fresh (09-28) exclusive: a top-tier producer backs a generative-AI feature adaptation, with a named director and AI vendor. It is a new project, unrelated to the Particle 6 'Storm Dogs' card (09-26) and the Zurich panel (09-28). Adds a news outlet to a mix that was mostly video and podcast.
